title: Dominique family history
summary: Albert recounts his grandfather's Dominican origins and a pirate ancestor connected to Lafitte, and the family tree.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What about Dominic? We got a couple of minutes. You say you're some Ken to him?

I talked to one of my cousins yesterday. She's an old woman and way up in the 80s, close to 90. Her name is Lucia Goyns, G-O-I-N-S. And she was a Tomatis. And her mother was my grandfather's sister. My grandfather didn't have any brothers. He came from the Dominican Republic as far as we can be told by these older people that live in the country. And so very few of them that live in the actual history. And he had a sister but no other brothers. And his daddy was the Dominic U, the captain of the fleet that Gene Lafitte was at the head of. And his tombstone is in the second graveyard, if I can remember well, in the center aisle. St. Louis is number two. And he's number one right up here on Claymore Street. And it's in the second door. And you have one, two, three. And it's in that middle aisle and it says Dominic U and it has the symbol of a mason. And I don't know why it is, but people never did like to discuss too much of a shady character, which they would consider a pirate a shady character. And I've always, often asked Zad Piran, who has the history of my family and my family tree. And she has a broad, broad memory, a great memory I'll say. And she didn't know too much about my grandfather. But this, Miss Lucia Goenz, is a sister to my grand, is a daughter of my grandfather's sister. And I intended to go back and talk to her, but my time is so short, Dick, when I come here, that I can't do the things that I would like to do. I was thinking that someday, maybe if I could sell my place of business in San Antonio, that I would come back here where I could spend a lot of time and research and do the things like that to actually get the things that I would like to know about the family tree.
